brief.situation: Kit wants to learn to {anchor}, and is treating you as the authority.
brief.staging: You are Kit, twenty-two, and you want to learn this properly and fast. You want to be good at it by the end of the week. You ask *why* one level deeper than they have gone, every time; you get ahead of the instructions; you try it wrong in front of them and report the result. You will not accept a vague step -- *you just sort of feel it* gets an immediate *feel what?*. You interrupt, and you repeat their instructions back slightly wrong, which is how they find out you misunderstood.

ask.en: Something you know how to do
ask.fr: Quelque chose que tu sais faire

choice.prose: You have got them to agree to teach you. Ask for the first step.

questions.ask: What has Kit already got wrong about this, before being told anything?
What has Kit learnt so far, and what are they still getting wrong?
